title: Security Alerting and Monitoring

header.html: 4.4 Explain security alerting and monitoring concepts and tools
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1What is monitored

Resource Examples
Systems Servers, endpoints, CPU, memory, disk, sign-ins
Applications Errors, transactions, access, performance
Infrastructure Network devices, firewalls, traffic, cloud services

2Monitoring activities

Activity Meaning
Log aggregation Collect logs from many sources into one place
Alerting Notify staff when a rule or threshold is met
Scanning Regular checks for vulnerabilities and drift
Archiving Keep logs for the required time (legal and investigation needs)
Reporting Summaries for managers and auditors
Alert tuning Adjust rules to cut false positives without missing real threats

Exam tip

. Too many false alarms cause alert fatigue, so teams tune alerts: raise thresholds, add context, remove duplicates. Aggregation allows correlation across sources.

3Tools

Tool What it does
Benchmarks Standard secure configurations (for example CIS) to measure against
Agents / agentless Agent-based collection uses software on the device (more detail); agentless collects remotely (nothing to install)
SIEM Security information and event management: collects, correlates and alerts on logs from many sources
Antivirus Detects and removes known malware
DLP Detects and blocks sensitive data leaving
Vulnerability scanners Find weaknesses
Orchestration Automates workflows across tools (SOAR, module 16)
Packet analyzer Captures and inspects network packets (for example Wireshark)

4Protocols and data sources

Item Meaning
NetFlow Summaries of network conversations (who talked to whom, how much)
SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol: monitors and manages network devices (use SNMPv3 for security)
syslog Standard way to send logs to a central server
SCAP Security Content Automation Protocol: standard formats to automate checking configuration and vulnerabilities
Port mirroring A switch copies traffic to a monitoring port (for IDS or analyzers)
Automated alerts Rule-based alerts by email, text or ticket
Dashboards Visual summary of status
Network management systems Central tools to monitor device health
Exam tip

. SIEM = collect, correlate, alert. NetFlow = traffic metadata, not content. Port mirroring (SPAN) feeds a sensor with a copy of traffic. syslog = log transport. SCAP = automation of compliance checks.

Exam tip

. A SIEM is only as good as the logs it receives and the rules that are tuned: collect from all key sources and tune alerts.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants logs from firewalls, servers and applications gathered in one place so that events can be correlated. What should it deploy?

  • AA captive portal
  • BA honeyfile
  • CA SIEM
  • DA wildcard certificate
Show the answer

Answer: C. A SIEM aggregates logs, correlates events and raises alerts.

S2Analysts ignore alerts because most are harmless. What activity should be performed?

  • ALog archiving
  • BAlert tuning
  • CPort mirroring
  • DVersion control
Show the answer

Answer: B. Tuning reduces false positives so real alerts are noticed.

S3A security team needs a copy of all traffic on a switch for an intrusion detection sensor. What should be configured?

  • ARate limiting
  • BDHCP snooping
  • CA VLAN trunk
  • DPort mirroring
Show the answer

Answer: D. Port mirroring sends a copy of traffic to the monitoring port.

S4Which data source shows which hosts talked to each other and how much data moved, without storing packet content?

  • ANetFlow
  • BA memory dump
  • CA system image
  • DSurveillance footage
Show the answer

Answer: A. NetFlow records conversation summaries and metadata.

S5A company wants monitoring on laptops that gives detailed local data and works even when they are off the VPN. Which collection method fits?

  • AAgentless polling only
  • BPort mirroring
  • CAgent-based collection
  • DA packet analyzer on the core switch
Show the answer

Answer: C. An installed agent can collect detailed local data wherever the device is.

S6Which protocol sends log messages from devices to a central log server?

  • ASNMP trap only
  • Bsyslog
  • COCSP
  • DSAML
Show the answer

Answer: B. Syslog is the standard way to forward logs to a central server.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does a SIEM do?

Show the answer

Collects, correlates and alerts on logs from many sources.

R2What is alert tuning?

Show the answer

Adjusting alert rules to reduce false positives while catching real threats.

R3What does NetFlow provide?

Show the answer

Summaries of network conversations.

R4What is the difference between agent-based and agentless?

Show the answer

Agent-based uses software on the device; agentless collects remotely.

R5What is SCAP for?

Show the answer

Automating checks of configuration and vulnerabilities with standard formats.

R6What is log archiving for?

Show the answer

Keeping logs for the required time for investigations and compliance.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Scope systems, applications, infrastructure
Activities aggregation, alerting, scanning, archiving, reporting, alert tuning
Tools benchmarks, agents or agentless, SIEM, antivirus, DLP, scanners, orchestration, packet analyzer
Protocols and sources NetFlow (metadata), SNMP, syslog, SCAP, port mirroring, dashboards, network management systems
